title: Handley Page Halifax's BB373 and JB874
location_name: Hull Bridge, Tickton, near Beverley, East Riding of Yorkshire
memorial_details: A black granite tablet with the 78 Squadron crest is fixed to the east abutment of the footbridge over the Hull River in Tickton. The gold lettering records the collision, lists the dead and ends with the words 'one remaining survivor'. IWM lists 15 names; the inscription as transcribed on our record gives only ten of the dead.
inscription: Dedicated to the aircrew of 78 Squadron who lost their lives following a collision in fog between two Halifax bombers BB373 EY-K and JB874 EY-E over Hull Bridge, Tickton at 04:30 hours on 24th August 1943; names; ONE REMAINING SURVIVOR

sources.title: Handley Page Halifax's BB373 and JB874 (IWM WMR 98870)

Pilot Officer Edward Platt 137558, Navigator, 78 Squadron

narrative:
Two Halifax bombers of 78 Squadron, BB373 and JB874, took part in the Berlin raid on the night of 23/24 August 1943. Both had bombed and were coming back to Yorkshire when they were told to land away from base. The researcher's page says they were sent first to Leconfield and then on to Hutton Cranswick; the accident record card, quoted by CWGC, says they were diverted from Breighton because of poor weather. At about 04:30 they collided over Hull Bridge at Tickton, about two miles north-east of Beverley. The memorial inscription gives fog as the cause.

All eight men aboard BB373 died. They were pilot George Bell, second pilot Ronald Gilbert, engineer Albert Lester, navigator Edward Platt, bomb aimer William Clarke, wireless operator and gunner Arthur Lee, and air gunners David Walton and Robert Fletcher. Bell was a New Zealander and Walton an Australian; both are buried at Harrogate. Six of the seven aboard JB874 died: pilot Charles Keirl, engineer Ernest Scorey, navigator Harry Baylis, bomb aimer Henry Raymond Jones, wireless operator Charles Hilton and gunner Frederick Roberts. The seventh man, Sgt J. Greet, was seriously injured and spent about five years recovering. The researcher notes that 78 Squadron lost five aircraft and 31 airmen that night.

crew.fate: Survived: seriously injured, hospitalised, about five years recovering

external_narratives.summary: Our capture of the IWM entry. Gives the address on the east abutment of the footbridge over the Hull River, Weel Street, Tickton, East Riding of Yorkshire, and 15 names on the memorial.
Regional crash researcher's account of the collision, with a full table of the eight BB373 crew: rank, service number, age, home town and burial. The page title misprints the serial as BB393.
key_details: 78 Squadron lost five aircraft and 31 airmen that night

external_narratives.summary: Same researcher's page for JB874, with the seven-man crew table. Six died; Sgt J. Greet was seriously injured and spent about five years recovering. Does not name the BB373 crew.
key_details: Greet only survivor, no first name
two of the dead may have died of injuries

external_narratives.summary: CWGC story about Platt. Cites the accident record card: the aircraft were diverted from Breighton, Leconfield could not take them, and they collided on the way to Hutton Cranswick. Lists the BB373 crew.
key_details: family memorial at Bury Cemetery, Redvales

external_narratives.summary: Entry for the plaque at Hull Bridge. Lists the 14 dead and Sgt J. Greet as survivor. No county, builder, dedication date or custodian given; custodian field open for claiming.

cause_of_loss: Collision in fog over Hull Bridge, Tickton, at about 04:30 after being diverted to Hutton Cranswick
